text: I notice the newborn is presenting with bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance, which are concerning signs. To help narrow down the potential causes, can you tell me the baby's exact age in days and whether they have passed any meconium stools within the first 48 hours of life?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the infant passed any meconium stools since birth, and does the abdominal examination reveal a distended abdomen or palpable masses? I also need to know if there are any visible cutaneous stigmata of Down syndrome.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.
